history.dynasty: Built by Nepal King Mahendravir Vikram Sahdev (Mahendra Vikram Shah); date CONFLICT (verify): 17th century per one Wikipedia page, 16th century per another, 1523 in the infobox of the first
history.summary: Coordinates (25.81528, 84.73222) are from Wikipedia for this temple, not the map geocoder (rate-limited); web-corroborated, not field-verified. TOWN CLARIFIED: the CSV town 'Siwan' is the district headquarters; the temple is at Mehdar village, Siswan block, about 32-35 km south of Siwan town (pincode 841203). Mahendra Nath Temple (Mehdar Dham) is a large Shiva temple complex on the bank of Kamaldah (Kamal Dah / lotus pond) Lake, described as the largest Shiva temple complex in northwestern Bihar. Legend: the Nepalese king Mahendravir Vikram Sahdev, suffering from chronic skin disease (leprosy), stopped at Mehdar on his way to Kashi, washed in a pit by a peepal tree and was healed; Lord Shiva appeared in his dream instructing him to excavate beneath the tree, where a Shivling was uncovered, and the king built the temple and excavated the pond (52 bighas). Construction is in Lakhauri bricks and traditional mortar; the sanctum houses a swayambhu (self-manifested) Shivling; architecture described as a blend of Nagara and Vesara styles; the main temple carries a gold-plated kalash and trishul. Every year Mehadaar Mahotsav is celebrated on Mahashivratri by the Bihar government. In July 2022 a stampede-like incident during the Sawan Somwari rush reportedly killed one person and injured several.

name: Mahendra Nath Temple, Mehdar
town_description: Mehdar is a village in the Siswan block of Siwan district in western Bihar, about 32-35 km south of Siwan town. It is a temple town, known almost entirely for the Mahendra Nath (Mehdar Dham) Shiva temple complex and its large Kamaldah lake, which draws devotees from far-flung areas during Sawan and Mahashivratri.

travel.road: Reachable via Chainpur and the Siwan-Hasanpura-Siswan route; about 32 km by road from the Siwan district headquarters.
